subject: Combined Science
source: Edexcel (Pearson) GCSE (9-1) Combined Science 1SC0 specification (2016 onwards) — Y10 covered subset across Biology Topics 1–5, Chemistry Topics 1–4 and Physics Topics 1–7, with HT-only items flagged.

specPoints.specTitle: Biology — animal and plant cell structure; sub-cellular structures and their functions
Biology — eukaryotic vs prokaryotic cells; bacterial structure including plasmids
Biology — diffusion, osmosis and active transport; surface area to volume ratio
Biology — enzymes as catalysts; effect of temperature, pH, substrate concentration on rate of reaction
Biology — mitosis and the cell cycle; cell differentiation and stem cells
Biology — the nervous system, neurones and reflex arc; synaptic transmission (HT only — chemical synapse mechanism)
Biology — sexual and asexual reproduction; meiosis; DNA structure
Biology — genotype/phenotype/alleles; Punnett squares for monohybrid inheritance
Biology — natural selection and evolution; antibiotic resistance as evidence
Biology — communicable diseases (TB, cholera, malaria, HIV); body's defences and white blood cells
Biology — vaccination, antibiotics, antiviral drugs; antibiotic resistance and herd immunity
Chemistry — atoms, elements, compounds; mass number, atomic number, isotopes; Bohr model
Chemistry — periodic table; Group 1, Group 7 and Group 0 trends and reactions
Chemistry — ionic, covalent and metallic bonding; properties linked to structure
Chemistry — states of matter; pure substances and mixtures; separation techniques
Chemistry — acids, alkalis, pH; reactions of acids; neutralisation
Chemistry — reactivity series; displacement; oxidation/reduction in terms of electrons (HT only)
Chemistry — extraction of metals: reduction with carbon and electrolysis (e.g. aluminium from bauxite)
Chemistry — reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium (HT only — Le Chatelier reasoning)
Physics — distance, displacement, speed, velocity, acceleration; equations of motion (HT for v² = u² + 2as)
Physics — Newton's three laws of motion; F = ma applied to everyday contexts
Physics — stopping distance: thinking + braking; factors affecting each
Physics — momentum and conservation of momentum in collisions (HT only — force as rate of change of momentum)
Physics — energy stores, transfers, conservation; KE, GPE, work done, power
Physics — efficiency; ways of reducing wasted energy
Physics — renewable and non-renewable energy resources; advantages and limitations
Physics — waves: wavelength, frequency, period, amplitude, v = fλ; transverse vs longitudinal
Physics — reflection, refraction and absorption of waves at boundaries
Physics — electromagnetic spectrum and uses/dangers of each region
Physics — radioactive decay (alpha, beta, gamma); nuclear equations; half-life calculations
Physics — irradiation vs contamination; medical and industrial uses of radioactivity; precautions
Physics — solar system, life cycle of stars; red shift and Big Bang theory (HT only — quantitative red-shift reasoning)
